You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Fern Valve Works","question":"Can the review board close the leak-testing row for V31?","claims":{"A":"V31 was in lot R8.","B":"Valve V31 passed the helium leak test at 3 bar.","C":"V31 underwent a nitrogen test."},"handoff":"The review board is considering whether to close the leak-testing row for valve V31. Claim A that V31 was in lot R8 is contradicted by inspection records placing it in lot R6. Claim B that V31 passed a helium leak test at 3 bar remains unresolved because the QA email mentions a 3-bar test but does not confirm the gas used, and the archived gas field is blank. Claim C that V31 underwent a nitrogen test is well supported by rig output records. Given the uncertainty about the helium test and confirmed nitrogen test, the board should be cautious about closing the helium leak test row without further verification of the test gas used.","follow_up":{"S4":"an independently archived helium rig result records a passing 3-bar test on V31."}}

Claim B was previously unresolved but is now supported by the independent helium rig result in S4 confirming a passing 3-bar helium test.
